original_question: For Euclidean spaces R^n equipped with central symmetries, calculate or estimate the centerpole numbers c_r^λ(R^n) for various choices of the number of colors r, the threshold λ, and the dimension n.
target_in_paper: Section 10, Problem 10.9: the open problem asking for the calculation or evaluation of the Euclidean centerpole numbers c_r^λ(R^n), with context supplied by the definition of c_r^λ(X) at the start of Section 10 and the partial Euclidean results in Theorems 10.2 and 10.3.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct ambient space R^n, the relevant symmetry class (central symmetries), the correct invariant c_r^λ(R^n), and the paper's open-ended objective of calculating or estimating these numbers for varying parameters. That is very close to the exact Euclidean open problem stated in the paper.
missing_details: The paper defines c_r^λ(R^n) as a minimum cardinality: the least size of a set C of centers, not just an abstract numerical invariant.
R^n is being viewed as a symmetry measure space whose admissible symmetries are the central symmetries s_c(x) = 2c - x for c in R^n.
The underlying 'measure' here is asymptotic dimension, so the condition attached to λ is asdim(A) >= λ for the monochromatic symmetric set A.
The nearby discussion treats n as a positive integer and λ as a finite nonnegative integer; in the sentence immediately before Problem 10.9 the relevant range is 0 <= λ < n.
For the Euclidean problem the colorings are arbitrary r-colorings of R^n; the Borel-restricted variant is introduced only in other settings such as hyperbolic spaces.

Under the paper's normalization of asymptotic dimension, λ = 0 is the case of an unbounded monochromatic symmetric subset, which explains why Theorems 10.2 and 10.3 are the main nearby partial results.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should explicitly define what 'symmetric with respect to c' means, namely A = 2c - A.
refined_question: For integers n >= 1 and r >= 1 and a finite nonnegative integer λ < n, view R^n as a symmetry measure space whose admissible symmetries are the central symmetries s_c(x) = 2c - x (c in R^n) and whose measure is asymptotic dimension, normalized so that bounded sets have asymptotic dimension -1. Let c_r^λ(R^n) be the smallest cardinality of a set C subset R^n such that every r-coloring χ: R^n -> {0, ..., r-1} contains a monochromatic subset A subset R^n with A = 2c - A for some c in C and asdim(A) >= λ. Calculate or estimate c_r^λ(R^n) for various values of r and λ.
justification: The draft is closest to Section 10, Problem 10.9, not to the broader Problem 10.1 and not to the specific special case Problem 10.7. Section 10 first defines the general centerpole number c_r^λ(X) for a symmetry measure space, then immediately specializes the discussion to Euclidean spaces R^n with central symmetries and asymptotic-dimension measure. Theorems 10.2 and 10.3 summarize the only exact Euclidean values and bounds currently available nearby, essentially for the λ = 0 case, and the sentence just before Problem 10.9 says that the proof of Theorem 9.1 yields lower and upper bounds for c_r^λ(R^n) when λ is finite and 0 <= λ < n. So the paper-faithful stand-alone reformulation is exactly Problem 10.9 with those hidden definitions and quantifiers made explicit (Section 10, definition before Problem 10.1, p. 15; Theorems 10.2-10.3, pp. 15-16; Problem 10.9, p. 16; Section 9, Theorem 9.1, pp. 14-15).
